items.title: Positive transverse photon one-particle space
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the real momentum dot product and norm are those of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Explicitly extend the real dot product
complex-bilinearly to $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j$ for $a,b\in\mathbb C^3$.
Each complex fiber instead has the positive Hermitian pairing
$\langle a,b\rangle_2=\overline a\cdot b=\sum_j\overline a_jb_j$ and
norm $\|a\|^2=\sum_j|a_j|^2$; the displayed integral uses this pairing.
Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-complex-dimensional plane $\{a\in\mathbb C^3:\mathbf k\cdot a=0\}$ perpendicular to the real vector $\mathbf k$ in that Hermitian pairing; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

items.title: Charged gauge data and SI-natural conventions
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Use the fixed Minkowski coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, on an open coordinate domain $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with its standard topology. Each $x^a$ has unit metre. For a smooth scalar component $u:U\to\mathbb R$ or $u:U\to\mathbb C$, define $\partial_a u:=\partial u/\partial x^a$; thus $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ at fixed $\mathbf x$, $\partial_j=\partial/\partial x^j$ for $j=1,2,3$, and each $\partial_a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Raise derivative indices with $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$. The fields in this definition are smooth maps
$$\phi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbf A\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R^3),\qquad \psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4),\qquad \chi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R).$$
Define the lower-potential component maps $A_a:U\to\mathbb R$ by $A_0=-\phi/c$ and $A_j=\mathbf A_j$; collectively $(A_a)$ is the real covector potential in this chart. Then $F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a$ has smooth real component maps $F_{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$. The spinor is an ordinary commuting $\mathbb C^4$-valued map, not a tuple of Grassmann generators. Its Dirac adjoint is the smooth row-valued map $\bar\psi:=\psi^\dagger\beta:U\to(\mathbb C^4)^*$, using the fixed matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$. In fixed SI units, $\phi$ is in volts, each $A_a$ is in $\mathrm{T\,m}$, $\psi$ is assigned field dimension $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, and $\chi$ is in webers; these unit labels accompany the maps and do not identify $q$ with a measured charge. For periodic spatial domains, the same component and unit conventions apply to smooth periodic coordinate lifts, with the quotient domain specified by the item using them.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Here $D_a$ acts on $\psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4)$ by $(D_a\psi)(x)=\partial_a\psi(x)-ig a_a(x)\psi(x)$, again a smooth map $U\to\mathbb C^4$. Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For the real smooth gauge-parameter map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R$ in webers, put $\alpha:=\chi/S_0\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

items.title: No global continuous real polarization frame
items.design_state: Local A-page prerequisite added because the two-polarization example requires the no-global-frame result; complete proof reduces it to the published even-sphere theorem.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For $n\in S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $E_n=n^\perp=\operatorname{Ran}(I-nn^T)$ be the real transverse plane. There do not exist continuous maps $e_1,e_2:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ such that, for every $n$, $(e_1(n),e_2(n))$ is an orthonormal basis of $E_n$. A continuous real orthonormal polarization frame would in particular give a continuous nowhere-zero tangent vector field on $S^2$.

items.title: Lorenz auxiliary subsidiary null quotient
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use $\mathcal H_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. On $\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ define
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\epsilon(\mathbf k)^\dagger\eta\,\delta(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,\qquad \eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).$$
For $\mathbf k\ne0$, let $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and set
$$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon\in\mathcal K:-\epsilon^0+n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0\text{ a.e.}\},\qquad T\epsilon=\boldsymbol\epsilon-n\epsilon^0.$$
Then $\mathcal K_0$ is closed, $T:\mathcal K_0\to\mathcal H_T$ is bounded and onto, and
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\langle T\epsilon,T\delta\rangle_2\quad(\epsilon,\delta\in\mathcal K_0).$$
Its radical (the vectors pairing to zero with all of $\mathcal K_0$) is
$$\mathcal N=\ker T=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,n(\mathbf k)):b\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)\}.$$
Consequently $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ with the induced form is a positive Hilbert space isometric to $\mathcal H_T$. The form on the four-component auxiliary space is indefinite; only the subsidiary quotient is the positive physical one-particle space.

items.title: Smeared Coulomb photon operator distribution
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $j=(j_1,j_2,j_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R^3)$ and use $\mathcal H_T$ and $P_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. For $\omega=|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, define
$$g_j(\mathbf k)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}(2\omega)^{1/2}}\, P_T(\mathbf k)\int_{\mathbb R^4}j(x)e^{i\omega x^0-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,d^4x.$$
Then $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$. On the finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$, the smeared transverse potential is
$$A_T(j)=a(g_j)+a^\dagger(g_j).$$
Its matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology; it is an operator-valued distribution and does not assign a pointwise operator to $A_i(x)$. With $E_i=-\partial_0A_i$, the equal-time canonical commutator is the distribution
$$[A_i(0,\mathbf x),E_j(0,\mathbf y)] =-i\,P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla_{\mathbf x})\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y).$$

items.title: Newtonian off-diagonal kernel of the transverse projector
items.design_state: Local A-page prerequisite added because the Coulomb-potential counterexample needs the Fourier projector kernel; complete proof derives it by Abel regularization and identifies its Newtonian off-diagonal part.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $G(\mathbf x)=1/(4\pi|\mathbf x|)$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, interpreted as its locally integrable distribution, and use the Fourier convention
$$\widehat f(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}f(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad f(\mathbf x)=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\widehat f(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k.$$
Then $\mathcal F^{-1}(|\mathbf k|^{-2})=G$ distributionally. Consequently, for $P_{T,ij}(\mathbf k)=\delta_{ij}-k_i k_j/|\mathbf k|^2$,
$$P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla)\delta^3 =\delta_{ij}\delta^3+\partial_i\partial_jG.$$
For $\mathbf x\ne0$,
$$\partial_i\partial_jG(\mathbf x) =-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^3} +\frac{3x_ix_j}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^5}.$$
Thus the equal-time transverse-potential commutator of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] has this off-diagonal Newtonian kernel (with its stated factor $-i$). The identity is distributional at the origin; the displayed classical derivative formula is only asserted away from it.

items.title: Dirac gauge covariance, action and conserved current
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open, let each $a_a:U\to\mathbb R$
be a smooth real potential component, and let $\psi:U\to\mathbb C^4$
be a smooth commuting spinor. The real gauge parameter is a smooth
$\alpha:U\to\mathbb R$, and all fields, derivatives and compactly supported
smooth variations below are on this same $U$ (including $U=\mathbb R^4$). Use the symmetrized classical density
$$\mathcal L_D=\frac i2\{\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi-(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\}-\mu\bar\psi\psi,\qquad D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+ig a_a\bar\psi.$$
For compactly supported smooth variations, its spinor Euler equation is $(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi=0$ and its adjoint. The density is invariant under the gauge transformation in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On solutions,
$$\partial_a j^a=0,\qquad j^a=g\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi.$$
In SI variables the corresponding Hamiltonian density has the sign convention
$$\psi^\dagger\!\left[c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot(-i\hbar\nabla-q\mathbf A)+\beta mc^2+q\phi\right]\psi.$$
These are conditional variational identities for smooth commuting classical fields. They assert no global existence theorem for the coupled field equations, no quantum current product, and no empirical measurement.

items.title: Gauss multiplier and smooth periodic Coulomb solver
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval, with $t$ measured in seconds and $x^0=ct$, and let $T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ be the flat spatial torus with period $L>0$ metres and periodic coordinates $\mathbf x$. Take jointly smooth periodic maps
$$\mathbf A:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R^3,\qquad \phi:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R,\qquad ho:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf J:I	imes T_L^3	o\mathbb R^3.$$
Write $\dot{\mathbf A}:=\partial_t\mathbf A$ for the time partial derivative at fixed $\mathbf x$, and $\mathbf B:=
abla	imes\mathbf A$. All spatial differential operators below are the periodic coordinate derivatives, and each displayed spatial integral and Hamiltonian is evaluated at a fixed $t\in I$; the time argument is suppressed in the formulas. In SI units, $\mathbf A$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$, $\phi$ has unit $\mathrm V$, $ho$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, and $\mathbf J$ has unit $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. Thus $\dot{\mathbf A}$ and $
abla\phi$ both have unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{T\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and every term of the formal classical Lagrangian density has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Let $c>0$ have unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, let $\mu_0>0$ be the symbolic magnetic constant with unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, and put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with unit $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; no numerical value for these constants is adopted. Define the formal classical density
$$\mathcal L= rac{\epsilon_0}{2}|\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi|^2- rac1{2\mu_0}|
abla	imes\mathbf A|^2-ho\phi+\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf A.$$
The canonical momenta are $ oldsymbol\pi_A=\epsilon_0(\dot{\mathbf A}+
abla\phi)$, with unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, and $\pi_\phi=0$. Periodic integration by parts gives the fixed-time Hamiltonian
$$H(t)=\int_{T_L^3}\left( rac{| oldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\epsilon_0}+ rac{|\mathbf B|^2}{2\mu_0}+\phi(
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho)-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf Aight)d^3\mathbf x.$$
Variation of the multiplier $\phi$ imposes $
abla\cdot oldsymbol\pi_A+ho=0$. In Coulomb gauge $
abla\cdot\mathbf A=0$, this becomes $-\Delta\phi=ho/\epsilon_0$. At each fixed $t$, a smooth periodic solution can exist only if $\int_{T_L^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$. If $\int_{T_L^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)\,d^3\mathbf x=0$ for every $t\in I$, there is a unique jointly smooth periodic solution with zero spatial mean, whose Fourier coefficients are
$$\widehat\phi_0(t)=0,\qquad \widehat\phi_k(t)= rac{\widehatho_k(t)}{\epsilon_0|2\pi k/L|^2}\quad(k
e0),\qquad \widehatho_k(t)=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}ho(\mathbf x,t)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot\mathbf x/L}\,d^3\mathbf x.$$
For every $t\in I$ it satisfies
$$ rac{\epsilon_0}{2}\int_{T_L^3}|
abla\phi|^2\,d^3\mathbf x= rac12\int_{T_L^3}ho\phi\,d^3\mathbf x= rac{L^3}{2\epsilon_0}\sum_{k
e0} rac{|\widehatho_k(t)|^2}{|2\pi k/L|^2}\ge0.$$
This is a classical conditional solver for smooth periodic neutral data; it makes no claim about quantum density products or nonperiodic boundary conditions.

items.title: Finite-mode Dirac first-order constraint reduction
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the constants in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]], $\hbar>0$, and a finite integer $N\ge1$. Let the real configuration space be $Q=\mathbb R^{2N}$ with coordinates $(x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_N,y_N)$ and let $T^*Q\cong\mathbb R^{4N}$ have corresponding real canonical momentum coordinates $(P^x_1,P^y_1,\ldots,P^x_N,P^y_N)$. On real smooth functions define the canonical Poisson bracket
$$\{F,G\}=\sum_{j=1}^N\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^x_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^x_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial x_j}+\frac{\partial F}{\partial y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial P^y_j}-\frac{\partial F}{\partial P^y_j}\frac{\partial G}{\partial y_j}\right),$$
and extend it $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to complex-valued smooth functions on $T^*Q$. Define the complex coordinate notation
$$z_j=x_j+iy_j,\qquad \bar z_j=x_j-iy_j,\qquad p_j=\frac{P^x_j-iP^y_j}{2},\qquad \bar p_j=\frac{P^x_j+iP^y_j}{2}.$$
These definitions give
$$\{z_j,p_k\}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \{\bar z_j,\bar p_k\}=\delta_{jk},$$
with all other elementary brackets zero; the bracket is extended by bilinearity and the Leibniz rule. The first-order kinetic term $\frac{i\hbar}{2}\sum_j(\bar z_j\dot z_j-\dot{\bar z}_jz_j)$ gives primary constraints
$$C_j=p_j-\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bar z_j,\qquad \bar C_j=\bar p_j+\frac{i\hbar}{2}z_j.$$
In the order $(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N)$ their constraint matrix and inverse are
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\hbar I_N\\i\hbar I_N&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-iI_N/\hbar\\iI_N/\hbar&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Here, “second class” means that the constraint matrix $M_{AB}=\{\chi_A,\chi_B\}$ is invertible. Thus these constraints are second class. For a real smooth finite-mode Hamiltonian $H\in C^\infty(Q;\mathbb R)$, viewed as independent of the momenta, define the Wirtinger derivative
$$\frac{\partial H}{\partial\bar z_j}:=\frac12\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial x_j}+i\frac{\partial H}{\partial y_j}\right).$$
The Dirac bracket
$$\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_A\}(M^{-1})_{AB}\{\chi_B,G\}, \quad \chi=(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N),$$
satisfies $\{z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=-i\delta_{jk}/\hbar$ and $\{z_j,z_k\}_D=\{\bar z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=0$. For a real smooth finite-mode Hamiltonian $H(z,\bar z)$ the reduced equation is $i\hbar\dot z_j=\partial H/\partial\bar z_j$. These are ordinary commuting coordinates; they do not derive CAR by canonical quantization.

items.title: Photon quotient Lorentz representation and positive dynamics
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On the future null cone write $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$, $\omega=|\mathbf k|$, $\mathbf k\ne0$, and use the measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. The fiber $p^\perp/\mathbb Cp$ has the positive quotient form of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]]. Give the proper orthochronous Lorentz group its matrix topology: the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb R^{16}$ with Euclidean matrix norm $\|A\|_{\rm mat}=(\sum_{i,j=0}^3|A_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$. For each proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the action
$$[s(p)]\longmapsto[\Lambda s(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$$
is a unitary representation on the square-integrable quotient sections. It is strongly continuous for this topology, meaning $\|U_\Lambda s-U_{\Lambda_0}s\|\to0$ for every section $s$ as $\|\Lambda-\Lambda_0\|_{\rm mat}\to0$. Its bosonic Fock lift is strongly continuous for the same topology. Under the unitary identification with $\mathcal H_T$ given by
$T_p[\epsilon]:=\boldsymbol\epsilon-(\mathbf k/\omega)\epsilon^0$
and $u(\mathbf k)=T_p[s(p)]/\sqrt{2\omega}$, as in [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]], the free translation representation for $a=(a^0,\mathbf a)\in\mathbb R^4$ has phase $e^{i(\omega a^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a)}$. Its bosonic Fock lift has the joint PVM $\mathsf E$ whose $n$-particle sector acts by multiplication by $\mathbf1_{\{(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_{r=1}^n\mathbf k_r)\in B\}}$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; on the vacuum it acts by $\mathbf1_B(0)$. Define its joint spectrum to be
$$\operatorname{supp}(\mathsf E):=\{q\in\mathbb R^4:\mathsf E(U)\ne0\text{ for every open neighborhood }U\text{ of }q\}.$$
Then this joint spectrum is the closed future cone
$$\overline V_+=\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\},$$
with the vacuum at $(0,\mathbf0)$. In the product realization of the sectors in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]], on sector $n$ the energy operator multiplies by $\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ and has the exact maximal domain
$$D(H_E)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|\right)^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
with the vacuum component unrestricted; here $\Psi_n$ is the symmetric transverse wavefunction in the product realization and the norm is the product-fiber Hilbert norm. Each momentum operator $P_j$ multiplies by $-\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}$ and has maximal domain
$$D(P_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left|\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}\right|^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
again with unrestricted vacuum component. These are mathematical free-field representation statements.

items.proof:
**Given:** [A1], [F1]–[F11], the future-cone parametrization, and the componentwise Lorentz action.

1.1 By [F5], $\Lambda$ preserves $\eta$ and sends a future null vector $p$ to a future null vector $\Lambda p$. It maps $p^\perp$ onto $(\Lambda p)^\perp$ and $\mathbb Cp$ onto $\mathbb C\Lambda p$, so it induces a well-defined map on the quotient fiber. The induced form is preserved because $\eta(\Lambda v,\Lambda w)=\eta(v,w)$; hence the fiber map is an isometry. The map $T_p$ is independent of the representative: replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon+cp$ changes its value by $c(\mathbf k-(\mathbf k/\omega)\omega)=0$. For $\epsilon\in p^\perp$, $\mathbf k\cdot T_p[\epsilon]=0$; its pairing is the positive quotient pairing of [F1]. The lift $\epsilon=(0,\sqrt{2\omega}\,u(\mathbf k))$ for transverse $u$ proves surjectivity, and $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$ gives $\int\|T_p[s(p)]\|^2d\nu=\int\|u(\mathbf k)\|^2d^3\mathbf k$. Thus the stated section identification is well-defined and unitary. Applying two Lorentz maps successively gives the representation composition law. [F1, F5, given, algebra]

1.2 The component identification of [F3] uses $X=\mathbb R^3\times\{1,2,3\}$ with Lebesgue measure times counting measure; $X$ is sigma-finite because the boxes $[-m,m]^3\times\{1,2,3\}$ have finite measure by [F8]. The finite measurable map $\boldsymbol\omega(\mathbf k,j)=(|\mathbf k|,-\mathbf k)$ lets us apply [F3]. It gives the PVM $\mathsf E(B)$ whose $n$-particle multiplier is $\mathbf1_{\{(\sum_r|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_r\mathbf k_r)\in B\}}$, with vacuum multiplier $\mathbf1_B(0)$, and it gives the maximal componentwise multiplier domains. By [F7], $P_T(\mathbf k)$ is pointwise self-adjoint and idempotent, so it commutes with each scalar multiplier; its tensor powers commute with the n-particle PVM and multiplier. The symmetric transverse sector is reducing, so restriction preserves the maximal domain, which for the energy is exactly $D(H_E)$ displayed in the Statement. [A1, F3, F7, F8, given, algebra]

2.1 For the boost $B_n(\chi)$ in [F2], put $\beta=\tanh\chi$ and $\gamma=\cosh\chi$, so $|\beta|<1$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$. In Euclidean unit direction $n$ [F5], its spatial cone coordinates satisfy
$$\mathbf k'=\mathbf k+(\gamma-1)(n\cdot\mathbf k)n+\gamma\beta\omega n,\qquad \omega'=\gamma(\omega+\beta n\cdot\mathbf k).$$
Taking $n$ as the third coordinate axis, the first two spatial coordinates are unchanged and
$$\frac{\partial k'_3}{\partial k_3} =\gamma\left(1+\beta\frac{k_3}{\omega}\right)=\frac{\omega'}{\omega}.$$
Thus $\det(\partial\mathbf k'/\partial\mathbf k)=\omega'/\omega$. A rotation has determinant one and preserves $\omega$. By [F2], every proper orthochronous $\Lambda$ is a product of these, so $d^3\mathbf k'/(2\omega')=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. Combining this change of variables with the fiber isometry in step 1.1 proves unitarity on the quotient-section space and verifies the stated identification with $\mathcal H_T$. [F2, F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 Each joint multiplier value $(\sum_r|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_r\mathbf k_r)$ lies in $\overline V_+$ by the triangle inequality [F9], so the PVM vanishes outside that closed cone. Fix a nonzero $\mathbf k_0$ and the boundary point $(|\mathbf k_0|,-\mathbf k_0)$. Choose $v\in\mathbb R^3$ not parallel to $\mathbf k_0$. By [F7], $P_T(\mathbf k_0)v\ne0$, and continuity gives a bounded open momentum neighborhood $V$ of $\mathbf k_0$, disjoint from zero, on which $\|P_T(\mathbf k)v\|$ is bounded below by a positive constant. Given any open neighborhood $G$ of $(|\mathbf k_0|,-\mathbf k_0)$, shrink $V$ so the map $\mathbf k\mapsto(|\mathbf k|,-\mathbf k)$ sends $V$ into $G$. Choose a ball inside $V$ and a positive finite-measure box $Q$ inside that ball by [F8]. The vector $u(\mathbf k)=\mathbf1_Q(\mathbf k)P_T(\mathbf k)v$ is a nonzero element of $\mathcal H_T$ supported over $G$, so $\mathsf E(G)u=u\ne0$. The vacuum supplies the origin. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, F9, step 1.2, given, construct]

3.1 Matrix multiplication is continuous, and the Lorentz equation gives $\Lambda^{-1}=\eta\Lambda^T\eta$, so inversion is continuous in the stated matrix topology. For $v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ with support in $B_R$, $R\ge1$, take the four-component representative $s_v(p)=(0,\sqrt{2\omega}\,P_T(\mathbf k)v(\mathbf k))$; under the stated unitary identification its class corresponds to $u=P_Tv\in\mathcal H_T$. Put $q=\Lambda^{-1}p$ and $a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)=T_p\Lambda(0,\sqrt{2q^0}\,P_T(\mathbf q)v(\mathbf q))$, the transverse chart representative of the transformed quotient section. If $\Lambda$ is sufficiently close to $I$, uniformly for future null $p$ one has $\omega/2\le q^0=|\mathbf q|\le2\omega$ and $\|\Lambda\|_{\rm op}\le2$: use $\|p\|_2=\sqrt2\omega$, the displayed inverse formula and the Euclidean Cauchy–Schwarz bound for a matrix acting on a vector. Thus $a_\Lambda$ vanishes outside $B_{2R}$, and $\|T_p\|_{\rm op}\le\sqrt2$, $\|P_T\|_{\rm op}\le1$ give $|a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)|\le C M\sqrt\omega$, where $M=\sup|v|$ and $C$ is independent of sufficiently small $\Lambda-I$. Consequently $|a_\Lambda-a_I|$ is bounded by a fixed constant $C_R M$ on the common support. Its squared $L^2(d\nu)$ contribution on $B_\delta$ is at most $C_R^2M^2\nu(B_\delta)=C_R^2M^2\pi\delta^2$ by [F6, F10]. On the annulus $\delta\le|\mathbf k|\le2R$, extend the explicit formula to matrices $A$ in a sufficiently small closed Euclidean matrix box about $I$ by putting $q=\eta A^T\eta p$. On that box $q^0$ and $|\mathbf q|$ remain positive, bounded away from zero on the annulus; the formula using $P_T(\mathbf q)=I-(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)^T$ is therefore continuous. The box times annulus is closed bounded in $\mathbb R^{19}$, hence compact, and [F11] gives uniform continuity of this formula there. Restricting back to Lorentz matrices yields $a_\Lambda\to a_I$ uniformly on the annulus, which has finite $\nu$-measure by [F6]. First choose $\delta$, then $\Lambda-I$, to obtain $\|a_\Lambda-a_I\|_{L^2(d\nu)}\to0$; this is exactly the quotient-section norm. No fiber value at the omitted apex is used. These sections are dense by [F4, F7]: approximate any $u\in\mathcal H_T$ by smooth compactly supported $v$ and project by $P_T$. Unitarity from step 2.1 gives $\|U_\Lambda s-s\|\le2\|s-s_v\|+\|U_\Lambda s_v-s_v\|$, extending continuity to every section. At any $\Lambda_0$, the representation identity reduces continuity to $U_{\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda}\to I$, and $\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda\to I$ in the matrix topology. For an elementary $n$-tensor, telescoping and unitarity give $\|(U_\Lambda^{\otimes n}-I)(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n)\|\le\sum_{j=1}^n\|(U_\Lambda-I)h_j\|\prod_{l\ne j}\|h_l\|\to0$. Finite linear combinations are dense in the Hilbert tensor product; the symmetric projection is a contraction commuting with the tensor action, so continuity holds on each symmetric sector. The vacuum is fixed. Truncating an arbitrary Fock vector to finitely many sectors leaves an error bounded by twice its tail norm under these unitary maps; letting that tail tend to zero proves strong continuity on all Fock space. [A1, F1, F4, F5, F6, F7, F9, F10, F11, step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Fix $(E,\mathbf P)$ with $E>|\mathbf P|$. Choose a unit $n\perp\mathbf P$; if $\mathbf P\ne0$, select a standard basis vector $w$ not parallel to $\mathbf P$ and normalize $w-(w\cdot\mathbf P/|\mathbf P|^2)\mathbf P$, while if $\mathbf P=0$ take any standard basis vector. Put $q=\tfrac12\sqrt{E^2-|\mathbf P|^2}$ and let $\mathbf k_1=-\mathbf P/2+qn$, $\mathbf k_2=-\mathbf P/2-qn$. Since $n\cdot\mathbf P=0$, $|\mathbf k_i|^2=|\mathbf P|^2/4+q^2=E^2/4$, so they are distinct nonzero momenta with $|\mathbf k_1|+|\mathbf k_2|=E$ and $-(\mathbf k_1+\mathbf k_2)=\mathbf P$. Given any open neighborhood $G$ of $(E,\mathbf P)$, continuity of the two-particle sum map gives disjoint bounded momentum neighborhoods $V_1,V_2$ of $\mathbf k_1,\mathbf k_2$ whose pairwise sums map into $G$. Choose fixed $v_i$ not parallel to $\mathbf k_i$ and shrink $V_i$ so $P_T(\mathbf k)v_i$ never vanishes there by [F7]; choose balls inside $V_i$ and positive finite-measure boxes $Q_i$ inside those balls by [F8]. The vectors $u_i(\mathbf k)=\mathbf1_{Q_i}(\mathbf k)P_T(\mathbf k)v_i$ are nonzero in $\mathcal H_T$. The symmetric vector $\Psi_2=P_{s,2}(u_1\otimes u_2)$ is nonzero because $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are disjoint, and its two-particle multiplier values lie in $G$. Hence $\mathsf E(G)\Psi_2=\Psi_2\ne0$. Thus every neighborhood of $(E,\mathbf P)$ has nonzero two-particle spectral projection. Together with steps 1.2–2.2 this proves $\operatorname{supp}(\mathsf E)=\overline V_+$; [F3] gives the exact energy domain from step 1.2. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, step 1.2, step 2.2, given, construct] ∎

items.title: Local covariant physical field-strength observables
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Work in the fixed length coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\eta(v,w)=-v^0w^0+\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf w$; write $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$. For subsets $S,T\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, say they are **spacelike separated** when $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2>0$ for every $x\in S$ and $y\in T$. Let $A_0=0$ and let $A_i$ be the transverse potential operator-valued distribution of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]]. Set
$$F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad E_i=-\partial_0A_i,\qquad B_i=\epsilon_{irs}\partial_rA_s,$$
where $\epsilon_{irs}$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. In the commutator formulas below, $\Delta=\sum_{r=1}^3\partial_r^2$ is the spatial Laplacian acting on $x-y$.
For a real antisymmetric test tensor $h=(h^{ab})$ with $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ and $h^{ab}=-h^{ba}$, define
$$F(h)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}F_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x =-A_b(\partial_a h^{ab}).$$
The effective test is conserved, $\partial_b\partial_a h^{ab}=0$, and $F(h)$ is unchanged by $A_b\mapsto A_b+\partial_b\lambda$ for smooth $\lambda$. Its one-particle coefficient $g_h$ is the vector $g_j$ of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] for $j_i=-\partial_a h^{ai}$, so $F(h)=a(g_h)+a^\dagger(g_h)$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$.

Let $C_0=-i\Delta_0$, where $\Delta_0$ is the massless scalar causal commutator of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. As distributions in $x-y$,
$$[E_i(x),E_j(y)]=[B_i(x),B_j(y)] =(-\delta_{ij}\Delta+\partial_i\partial_j)C_0(x-y),$$
$$[E_i(x),B_j(y)]=\epsilon_{jri}\partial_0\partial_rC_0(x-y).$$
Every right-hand side has support in the closed causal cone. Hence compactly supported tests whose supports are spacelike separated in the stated Minkowski sense give commuting field-strength operators on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The quotient representation of [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]] makes these smeared field strengths Lorentz covariant: their on-shell coefficient depends on a polarization class only through $p_a\epsilon_b-p_b\epsilon_a$. These conclusions concern gauge-invariant free observables and do not assert locality of the Coulomb potential.

items.title: Bounded local photon Weyl observable algebra
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the Minkowski coordinates and separation condition of [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]], so $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2$. Use the Hilbert space and projection of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]: $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$ with pairing $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int\overline u\cdot v\,d^3\mathbf k$, the matrix $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-nn^T$ for $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, and its bounded multiplication operator $M_{P_T}:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$, $(M_{P_T}u)(\mathbf k)=P_T(\mathbf k)u(\mathbf k)$. The value at zero is immaterial in $L^2$, and $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}=\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ a.e.}\}$ has the inherited Hilbert pairing. A spacetime region $O$ means an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ in its standard topology. A real antisymmetric test $h=(h^{ab})$ is supported in $O$ when each component $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ has support contained in $O$. Two open regions $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated when $\eta(x-y,x-y)>0$ for every $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$. Let $g_h\in\mathcal H_T$ be the one-particle vector for such a test from [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]]. The space $\mathcal H_T$ is separable in its Hilbert norm topology: it is the range of $M_{P_T}$ on the separable space $\mathcal H$. Define
$$W_O(h)=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h),$$
where $W_{\rm Segal}$ is the Weyl unitary of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. It is bounded and unitary, and its one-parameter group has the self-adjoint field-strength closure as generator. For every open region $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, let $\mathcal A(O)$ be the norm-closed unital $*$-algebra generated by $W_O(h)$ for real antisymmetric tests supported in $O$; equivalently its bounded real and imaginary parts are included as observables. If $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated by the stated Minkowski condition, then $\mathcal A(O_1)$ and $\mathcal A(O_2)$ commute.

items.title: Two physical photon fibers without global frame
items.design_state: Assigned QFT-MG01 research interface authored as a conditional mathematical item with exact hypotheses and a complete local proof.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For each nonzero $\mathbf k$, the physical photon fiber is the real plane $n^\perp$ (or its complexification), where $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$, and therefore has dimension two. Locally in direction space one can choose two continuous orthonormal polarization vectors. There is no continuous real orthonormal polarization frame on all of $S^2$. The global subsidiary quotient $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]] is isometric to the transverse space $\mathcal H_T$ of square-integrable sections from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. At a fixed direction $n$, the auxiliary fiber $K_{0,n}=\{(a,v)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb C^3:n\cdot v=a\}$, with form $[(a,v),(b,w)]_\eta=-\overline a b+\overline v\cdot w$, has radical $N_n=\mathbb C(1,n)$ and quotient isometric to the complex transverse plane. Thus four auxiliary components do not represent four positive physical polarizations; the global section space is not a single fiber.
